During the course of the inquest I heard evidence from GP Partner at the Collingwood Health Group who [REDACTED] informed me that GP practice records do not include an alert from EMIS or System 1 IT systems to provide an automatic flag on a patient's GP medical records if they are classed as a non-responder for a smear test by the National Screening Service.
lack of automatic flag for non-responder smear test patients

The alert system is only triggered after a patient attends a smear test. For a non-responder, they go back into the three or five year waiting list for a National Screening invitation for a smear test.

An automatic flag or alert when a patient fails to attend for a smear test as part of the National Screening Service, would mean that a GP surgery would not have to manually add a warning as an entry onto an individual's GP records. It would standardise the approach across all GP surgeries and could increase patient safety.

the system does not have a scheduled task feature which would allow the GP to create an alert on a patient's record to flag up when a task is due at a future date - eg an alert to book a follow up scan in one year
